evidence.reason: The target is partitioned by symbol, both sides are sorted by UTC timestamps, and merge_asof uses direction=backward at lines 352-376. The join therefore only selects an available_at timestamp less than or equal to the target timestamp.

The production enrich_target_frame path is exercised with a target immediately before, at, and after release; the test requires NaN before release and 0.5 at and after release at lines 96-98. A duplicate available_at row in a supplied feature frame is not rejected at onchain_pipeline.py:363-368 and could select an unintended equal-time value, but it cannot make that value visible before its release time.

The normal enrichment path preserves the copied target and appends the missing ONCHAIN_FEATURE_NAMES in registry order at lines 387-455. However, the required no-change invariant is not fail-closed: numeric originals are accepted through np.allclose with rtol=1e-5 at lines 464-475. For example, a 100000.0 OHLCV value changed to 100000.5 is accepted.

New feature values are converted with errors=coerce and then dropna at lines 488-495. A staged value such as 'not-a-number' is silently treated as an allowed missing warm-up value instead of being rejected, so exact twelve-column output does not prove valid feature values.
The hashed contract includes registry_version, sorted source/target/output hash maps, feature_names, coverage, funding_gap, and build_parameters at lines 533-545.

created_at is emitted only in the outer manifest at lines 547-560 and is absent from contract before contract_digest is calculated. The end-to-end test also obtains the same contract_digest on a repeat build at tests/unit/test_onchain_dataset_builder.py:261-272. A registry field edit without a version bump would not be represented, but the stated v1 contract requires the registry version and the CLI passes the frozen version explicitly.

The CLI writes both staging files and re-reads them before verification at lines 200-206, so the tested forced verification failure reaches no replacement and leaves the train bytes unchanged at tests/unit/test_onchain_dataset_builder.py:155-175.

The replace branch performs two independent os.replace calls at lines 255-257, with no rollback. If the second call fails, the train original has already been replaced while the test original remains unchanged. Also, the no-replace custom-output branch still calls os.replace at lines 258-262 despite the replace-only-with-flag contract.

The documented direct command executes this file, but it imports gpu_fuzzy_trader before adding the repository root to sys.path. In a clean checkout without an installed package, direct CLI execution can fail before staging starts.

checks.evidence: The basic backward join and manifest contract are present, but the verification gate accepts small numeric mutations and malformed on-chain strings (gpu_fuzzy_trader/data/onchain_pipeline.py:464-495), verify-only is fail-open for non-canonical shapes (scripts/build_onchain_dataset.py:44-61), and the two-file replacement has no rollback (scripts/build_onchain_dataset.py:255-257).

The new tests call builder.main in-process and monkeypatch verify_staged_dataset for the failure case at tests/unit/test_onchain_dataset_builder.py:155-175, so they do not catch the documented direct-script import failure. The full CLI fixture has only 16 intraday and 10 daily source observations at lines 76-80, below the warm-up minima, and does not exercise finite generated features. There are no tests for malformed feature text, tolerated original mutations, non-canonical verify-only shapes, or failure of the second replacement.

The BASE..HEAD tracked diff is limited to the four package files. Inbound graph tracing found the new enrichment and verification symbols called only by this new CLI and its tests; no existing production caller depends on them. The index has no recorded issue for the changed source paths, although data/train_new.csv is a separate skipped parse-timeout path and was not changed.

The onchain_pipeline change is append-only after the approved unit-1 code, and .gitignore changes only target the requested on-chain source and staged CSV artifacts. The implementation remains within the unit-2 file scope.

findings.title: Direct CLI execution can fail before the builder starts
findings.description: The documented invocation runs scripts/build_onchain_dataset.py directly. The file imports gpu_fuzzy_trader before inserting the repository root into sys.path. This repository has no packaging metadata that guarantees the checkout is installed in the venv, so a clean direct invocation can raise ModuleNotFoundError. Add the same project-root setup used by the other direct scripts, before the package imports.

findings.title: Two target replacements are not transactionally atomic
findings.description: The train os.replace completes before the test os.replace. A permission error, missing destination, or other filesystem error on the second call leaves train replaced and test original, which corrupts the paired canonical tapes. Use a rollback/publication strategy and add a test that forces the second replace to fail.

findings.title: No-replace custom outputs still use os.replace
findings.description: The no-replace branch calls os.replace for custom outputs at lines 258-262. This violates the stated os.replace-only-with---replace contract, even though it does not replace the source paths. Write the requested outputs without this replacement operation, or define and test a narrower exception in the contract.

findings.title: Original-value verification allows material mutations
findings.description: np.allclose(..., rtol=1e-5, atol=1e-8) is used for every numeric original column. It accepts changes such as 100000.0 to 100000.5, so the OHLCV and eighteen-feature immutability gate is not exact. Compare the parsed values exactly after the CSV round trip, with an explicit policy for the permitted serialization representation.

findings.title: Malformed on-chain values are coerced into accepted NaNs
findings.description: The staged verifier coerces invalid feature text with errors=coerce and then drops it. A corrupt value can therefore evade both the finite-range check and the expected numeric feature contract. Reject non-numeric/non-finite values explicitly while allowing only actual missing warm-up values.

findings.title: verify-only does not enforce the dataset shape or manifest
findings.description: The 37-column check is conditional on both exact canonical row counts. A truncated dataset, or a small file with only datetime/symbol and twelve on-chain columns, passes the checks at lines 44-54. Extra/missing base or legacy columns are not checked, and a missing manifest is silently accepted at line 63. Enforce the expected row counts and exact ordered 37-column contract, and require/validate the manifest when verify-only is requested.

findings.title: Tests miss the important CLI and verification failure paths
findings.description: The tests invoke main in-process, use a monkeypatched verifier for atomic failure, and use source fixtures too short to produce finite transformed values. Add a subprocess/direct-entrypoint test plus malformed-feature, exact-original-value, verify-only shape, and second-replace failure tests.

findings.title: Custom staging failures leave unignored .tmp artifacts
findings.description: Custom output paths stage to <output>.tmp at lines 189-195. If verification or a later operation fails, that file remains, while .gitignore:346-349 does not ignore the .tmp suffix. Use unique temporary files with cleanup or add a narrowly scoped ignore rule.

notes: The tracked scope is bounded and the package's targeted tests pass, with the two unrelated baseline failures waived as documented. The basic backward join and clock-excluded manifest are sound. Approval is blocked by the direct CLI import hazard, fail-open verification, weak verify-only shape gate, and replacement failure path. Untracked .antigravity/.opencode harness artifacts were treated as non-blocking scratch and are not part of the tracked review.
